subject: Re: Custom SLA & order form language for enterprise deployment
messages:
From: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@aureliatx.com>
To: procurement@aureliatx.com, karty@[redwoodinternal] <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@aureliatx.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum + order form language (MSA attachments)

Karthik / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but have a few contract-level asks before procurement can sign the order form and attach the SOW to our enterprise MSA. Please find our redlines attached (Aurelia_MSA_redline_20260602.pdf). High level asks: 

- Uptime: We need a clear uptime commitment for the dedicated inference endpoints serving our production models. We requested 99.99% monthly availability, with defined measurement windows and credits.
- Latency SLOs: P95 and P99 latency commitments for 512-token generation profiles (we provided sample traffic in the XLSX).
- Exception carve-outs: planned maintenance windows, emergency security patches, force majeure, networking outside Redwood control — we need the language to be explicit.
- Remedies: service credits scaled by downtime minutes; 30-day cure period and defined escalation path.
- Order form: explicit line items for Dedicated GPU reservation size, minimum commit term, and early termination language; want to see specific wording we expect in the order form so our procurement can approve the SOW attachment.

Can you provide a proposed SLA addendum (redline-friendly DOCX) and suggested order form wording that maps to your Dedicated product? Also confirm what evidence you can provide (uptime dashboards, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts) and the standard lead time for Dedicated provisioning.

Thanks,
Marco Diaz
IT Ops Manager
Aurelia Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@aureliatx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum + order form language (MSA attachments)

Marco — thanks for the clear summary and the attached redlines. Looping in Marissa (Legal lead on enterprise SOWs) and Ben (Solution Architect) to help with technical SLO language and the order form mapping.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provide uptime dashboards and token-level latency breakdowns, plus a SOC2 report under NDA.
- Dedicated capacity provisioning lead time: typically 3–4 weeks after order + capacity confirmation; can prioritize if you need an accelerated window.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa will review your MSA redlines and propose narrow addendum language for the SLA definitions and remedies.
2) Ben will draft an order form snippet that maps to Dedicated SKU names, reserved GPU counts, and billing cadence.
3) I'll put together a draft SLA addendum (based on Redwood template) and call out any exceptions that we need to negotiate (planned maintenance windows, fault domains, third-party network outages).

Can you confirm the measurement region (us-west-2 vs multi-region) and whether the latency samples in the XLSX are for real-time inference (streaming) or batch? That will change the P95/P99 baselines we propose.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@aureliatx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@aureliatx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum + order form language (MSA attachments)

Karthik / team — thanks. A few clarifications:
- Measurement region: production workloads will be in us-west-2 initially; we'll evaluate multi-region later.
- Latency profile: these are interactive inference requests (streaming responses to end-users). Our sample workload shows median payloads ~200 tokens; we've included spike patterns in the XLSX.
- Availability expectation: procurement prefers 99.99% monthly availability for Dedicated. If Redwood has a standard differentiation between Hosted vs Dedicated, please call that out in your proposal.
- Remedies: prefer service credit ladder (e.g., 99.9–99.99 = X, below 99.9 = Y) and a maximum credit cap tied to monthly recurring fees.

Also, Sofia (Legal) will want a short turnaround on the redline (5 business days) to meet our internal board sign-off schedules. Can you confirm your team's turnaround and whether you can provide an editable DOCX?

Regards,
Marco

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@aureliatx.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: custom SLA addendum + order form language (MSA attachments)

Marco / Sofia — thanks for the deadline note. Attached is a draft SLA addendum (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_template_20260605.docx) and an order form snippet below that maps to the Dedicated offering. The draft is intentionally conservative and framed for redline; please feel free to mark changes directly. We can turn around a redline within 3 business days if the changes are limited to numeric SLO/remedy values.

Key proposed items (high-level):
- Availability definitions:
  • "Monthly Availability" measured as (Total Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month for the specific Dedicated cluster(s) assigned to the account.
  • Proposed commitments: Hosted API (non-dedicated): 99.90% monthly availability; Dedicated Reserved Capacity: 99.99% monthly availability.
- Latency SLOs (for interactive streaming inference, 512-token baseline):
  • P95 (steady-state) <= 350 ms
  • P99 <= 900 ms
  • Measurement: service-side server-to-client token lag, averaged across the Dedicated cluster and reported monthly.
- Exceptions/Exclusions: Planned maintenance (scheduled with >=72 hours notice), Customer-induced outages, third-party network outages, force majeure, and actions required by law. Planned maintenance windows up to 4 hours/month excluded from downtime.
- Remedies: tiered service credit schedule tied to Monthly Availability for the Dedicated cluster: 
  • >=99.99%: no credit
  • 99.95% - 99.989%: 10% of monthly Dedicated charge
  • 99.0% - 99.949%: 25% of monthly Dedicated charge
  • <99.0%: 50% of monthly Dedicated charge
  • Credit cap: 100% of monthly Dedicated charge per billing period. Credits are exclusive remedy.
- Cure & Escalation: 30-day cure period for non-security defects; immediate escalation path to Redwood account lead and engineering SREs for incidents impacting >10% of provisioned capacity.

Order form snippet (proposed language):
"Order Form: Dedicated Inference Reserved Capacity
- Product: Redwood Dedicated — Reserved Cluster
- SKU: RDW-D1-RESERVED (example)
- Quantity: 4 x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (custom sizing subject to final resource mapping)
- Term: 12 months (auto-renewal)
- Billing: Monthly in arrears
- Service Level: Dedicated Reserved Capacity — governed by the attached SLA Addendum (Exhibit A). Availability and latency commitments apply to the provisioned cluster identified on the Activation Schedule.
"

Evidence & artifacts: we will provide uptime dashboards (read-only link), per-token latency histograms for the Dedicated cluster, and SOC2 Type II report under an NDA.

Next steps:
- Marco / Sofia: please review the attached DOCX and mark any redlines.
- If Aurelia confirms the Dedicated sizing and the 99.99% target, Ben will produce an updated capacity and provisioning ETA (we can often provision within 2 weeks if capacity is available).
- Legal: if the remedy ladder or planned maintenance windows are a hard stop, call that out and we'll escalate to our Head of Legal for decision.

Attaching: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_template_20260605.docx (editable) and a sample OrderForm_Aurelia_20260607.docx stub for mapping.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Legal — Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
